display.title: Yud-Tes Kislev: Thankfulness, and the Alter Rebbe and the Miser's Coin
display.summary_short: On Yud-Tes Kislev a guest storyteller shares how thankfulness brings joy, and tells how the Alter Rebbe's thank-you for a tiny coin freed a captured groom.
display.summary_long: Visiting a group on Yud-Tes Kislev, the storyteller opens with a l'chaim and tells how, after a month in a coma with COVID, his family added a new name meaning life, and how he now thanks Hashem twice every morning. Thankfulness, he teaches, is the secret to always being happy: Tehillim 100 begins with thanks before 'serve Hashem with joy'; a man kept a list of everything he was grateful for; and whoever has eyes, teeth, hands and feet is truly rich. He explains that the Alter Rebbe was freed after answering the last question with a smile, and passes on the Rebbe's advice not to speak negatively even about yourself. The story: a Jew-hating official seizes an orphan groom on his wedding day for 25 years in the army and demands a thousand rubles. The Alter Rebbe visits the town's rich 'miser', accepts his tiny coin with a warm thank-you, and the man, deeply moved, explains why he stopped giving and pays the whole ransom. The wedding goes ahead, and the official's lost money ends up as the couple's gift.
display.lesson: Thankfulness brings joy, and accepting even a small gift with a warm thank-you can open a person's heart.
